advances: Local necessary condition for an attained planar compatible minimum with a stable positive-curvature arc and smooth selected cap masses. The multipliers depend on the selected exact covers.

proof:
Every finite set of changes in $U$ spans a feasible open coordinate chart about zero. On the compact union of their supports, the positive curvature radii and inactive Jensen gaps are bounded below. The changes have bounded second derivatives, and the active Jensen rows remain exact. The perturbed supports retain positive interior, for example by uniform convergence of the support functions and the old inballs. The old strict cap margins on the affected faces are uniform on those compact intervals. The planar quadratic area formula and strict-side cap localization in 6ae2eb173ed91aee therefore apply. In this smooth setting the displacement on a changed arc is $t(\delta h_z u+\delta h_z' u')$ and the changed boundary portions stay on the old side. The same area difference localized to a cap is its indicator times the fiber area difference.

Take $\delta h_z=v_z\phi$ with $v\in L$ and $\phi\in C_c^\infty(I)$ supported in a subinterval of length less than $\pi$. Require $\int r_z\phi=0$ for every $z$. There is a nonzero solution obtained from more disjoint smooth bumps than equations. The first fiber and cap masses vanish. Writing $Q(\phi)=\int(\phi^2-\phi'^2)$, the second total and cap masses at fixed thresholds are $Q(\phi)\sum_zv_z^2$ and $Q(\phi)\sum_z I_{ijz}v_z^2$. Dirichlet Poincaré gives $Q(\phi)<0$. At every selected deepest group the critical caps have old mass $\beta M$, fixed normals, and positive circuit weights balancing their continuous parts. The exact common-mass root of f73024c7ebf4e57f applies on this chart. The first threshold and common-mass velocities vanish, so its second-derivative and quotient formulas give
$$
D^2f_i[\delta h,\delta h]=(-Q(\phi))q_i(v).
$$
For a finite conic combination, place these bumps on pairwise disjoint short intervals and rescale each to give the specified $-Q(\phi)$, omitting zero coefficients. The first masses still vanish, and the quadratic area cross terms between distinct intervals are zero. This realizes the whole combination in one signed direction.

The chosen exact circuits and the persistent strict slack at the other sites meet 1fa8cb387c27b040. Thus $\max_i f_i$ is a touching upper comparison for actual normalized depth. If a vector in the stated cone had all coordinates negative, realize its conic part by $\delta h$ and its first-variation part by $a\in U$. The feasible path $h+t\delta h+t^2a/2$ has each $f_i$ equal to $\beta$ plus $t^2/2$ times its negative coordinate plus $o(t^2)$, contradicting local minimality. Separating the convex cone from the open negative orthant gives a nonzero nonnegative functional, nonnegative on the cone and zero on its first-variation subspace, which occurs in both signs. Normalize it to obtain $\pi$. The formula for $q_i$ gives the stated positive semidefinite form after multiplication by $M/\beta$.

For arbitrary $v\in L$ and compact smooth $\phi$, the first derivative formula for the same circuit root gives
$$
\sum_i\pi_i g_i(v\phi)=-(\beta/M)\int_I\phi(\theta)\sum_zW_zv_zr_z(\theta)\,d\theta.
$$
Its vanishing and continuity give $\sum_z W_zv_zr_z(\theta)=0$ pointwise for all $v\in L$. Applying $1+\partial_\theta^2$ to the active identities gives $r(\theta)\in L$. These are exactly the nullspace conditions. If the nullspace is a line, choose a spanning vector $a$ with all coordinates positive by evaluating $r$ at one angle. Then $r_z/r_{z_0}=a_z/a_{z_0}$ for any fixed $z_0$, so $h_z-(a_z/a_{z_0})h_{z_0}$ solves $f''+f=0$ on $I$ and is a translation term. In the source example $v=(a,b,(a+b)/2)$ and $W=(1,1,-2)$ give $\sum_zW_zv_z^2=(a-b)^2/2$, hence equal curvature radii on the null line.
statement:
Let a compatible family of positive planar convex bodies on a fixed finite integer base locally minimize maximal normalized mixed closed-halfspace depth, with value $\beta>0$ and summed area $M$. Fix an open normal interval $I$ on which every $h_z$ is $C^2$ and $r_z=h_z+h_z''>0$. Assume the active finite Jensen support rows are identically zero on $I$, with common coefficient kernel $L$, and the remaining rows have positive gaps on each compact subinterval used. Choose any exact positive critical circuit at each deepest base and a finite strict slack cover at the other bases. On each affected fiber suppose the entire exposed face for each angle in $I$ has a fixed strict side of each selected cap plane; let $I_{ijz}$ be the inside bit for cap $j$ of deepest group $i$ in fiber $z$. Assume the selected critical cap masses are $C^2$ in threshold and body parameters on the finite-dimensional arc charts below, with old $S_{ij}=-\partial_bF_{ij}>0$.

Let $U$ be the signed linear space of $L$-valued smooth support changes compactly supported in $I$. If $\rho_{ij}>0$ are the positive circuit coefficients, put $\theta_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/\sum_k(\rho_{ik}/S_{ik})$ and $c_{iz}=\sum_j\theta_{ij}I_{ijz}$. Write $f_i$ for the actual normalized common-mass circuit cover, $g_i=Df_i$ on $U$, and $q_i(v)=M^{-1}\sum_z(\beta-c_{iz})v_z^2$ for $v\in L$. Every finite conic combination of the vectors $q(v)$ is the joint Hessian of the $f_i$ in one feasible direction with zero first body and cap masses. The cone generated by the $q(v)$ plus $\{(g_i(a))_i:a\in U\}$ avoids the open negative orthant.

There is one probability vector $\pi$ on the deepest groups with $\sum_i\pi_i g_i=0$ on $U$ and $\sum_i\pi_iq_i(v)\ge0$ for all $v\in L$. For
$$
\lambda_{ij}=\pi_i\theta_{ij}/\beta,\qquad W_z=1-\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij} I_{ijz},
$$
one has $\sum_{ij}\lambda_{ij}=1/\beta$. The restricted quadratic form $\sum_zW_zv_z^2$ is positive semidefinite on $L$, and $r(\theta)$ belongs to its nullspace for every $\theta\in I$. A one-dimensional restricted nullspace forces fixed positive curvature ratios and locally homothetic arcs up to translations.
title: One second-order stress for all smooth compatible arc directions
